lines.text: Then $\sqrt{2} = \hl{1}{\frac{p}{q}}$ with $p, q$ integers having no common factor (the fraction is in simplest form).

steps.ask: Which assumption about the fraction does this break?
steps.title: Reach the contradiction

lines.text: $\hl{2}{p}$ and $\hl{3}{q}$ now have a common factor of $2$. This contradicts the assumption that they have no common factor.

lesson.note: The letters are a and b instead of p and q, and the squaring step is written out in full. The method is the same: assume a fraction in lowest terms, show both top and bottom are even, then contradict the lowest-terms assumption.
